name: Evan Koch
life: “I still remember hearing the first birds on the street during a power cut.” Tuesday often includes a stop at Ferris Deli, where Evan asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I work next door and hear the spinners every day. On the quiet morning I heard a bird in our passage for the first time.
appearance: Evan has a blunt cut just below the ears, a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, and a favorite piece of clothing, a striped cotton shirt. It usually goes with a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. When somebody else has the floor, Evan draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first.
personality: Evan is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Evan is concerned.
agenda: To enjoy the newly audible birds on the quiet morning.
family: Jody Ito is Evan’s cousin raised in the same household. Evan chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Jody brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *Care with a clock*, Jody says, “I wrote the billing software and never watched somebody fasten a row of small buttons.”
connections: Victor Blair. A familiar warm shirt is one of the few things the neighbor misses in the sudden quiet.

reactions.situation: The operator closes the doors for a family birthday
reactions.response: Evan looks for a neighboring wash service and leaves the family birthday intact.

reactions.situation: Someone offers a cash reward for naming a rumored culprit
reactions.response: Evan keeps the money and the rumor out of the conversation and shares only firsthand observations with the person taking the report.
